settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: RequestBuilder.addPathParam does apply canonicalizeForPath to the value (RequestBuilder.java:94), so characters such as space, quotes, '<', '>', '^', '`', '{', '}', '|', '\', '?', '#' and, when not already encoded, '/' and '%' are percent-encoded — limiting many injection forms.

The final URL is produced through OkHttp's HttpUrl APIs (baseUrl.newBuilder / urlBuilder.build / baseUrl.resolve, RequestBuilder.java:149, 189-197), and OkHttp performs its own path canonicalization; it is plausible that dot-segments are normalized rather than sent literally, which would reduce or remove the practical effect.

retrofit/src/main/java/retrofit2/RequestFactory.java, which parses the URL template and validates @Path parameter names against the template, was not among the read source spans, so template-side mitigations (if any) were not examined.
candidates.description: RequestBuilder.addPathParam builds the request relative URL by directly substituting the @Path value into the URL template: `relativeUrl = relativeUrl.replace("{" + name + "}", canonicalizeForPath(value, encoded));` (RequestBuilder.java:94). The only transformation applied to the value is character-level encoding in canonicalizeForPath (RequestBuilder.java:97-144), which percent-encodes control characters, characters in PATH_SEGMENT_ALWAYS_ENCODE_SET, and — only when alreadyEncoded is false — '/' and '%' (lines 101-103, 125-127). Dot characters ('.') are never in the encode set and are always passed through unchanged, and when alreadyEncoded is true (i.e. `@Path(..., encoded = true)`) slashes and percent signs are also passed through unchanged. Consequently a caller-supplied value such as ".." inserted into a template like "/api/{id}/data" yields "/api/../data", and with encoded=true a value containing "../" can introduce real path separators. The substituted string is later combined with the base URL: either via `baseUrl.newBuilder(relativeUrl)`/`urlBuilder.build()` (RequestBuilder.java:149-153, 189-193) or via `baseUrl.resolve(relativeUrl)` (RequestBuilder.java:197). There is no check in the read source that rejects dot-segments or traversal sequences before the URL is resolved, so a request intended for a path under the base prefix can be resolved to a different path. Untrusted input reaching this code requires the application to pass an attacker-influenced value to a `@Path` parameter (ParameterHandler.Path.apply -> builder.addPathParam, ParameterHandler.java:94-99). This is reported as a candidate; the amount of path manipulation actually preserved in the final request depends on URL canonicalization performed downstream in OkHttp/the server, which was not read.
missing_evidence: Behavior of OkHttp 3.11.0 HttpUrl.resolve / HttpUrl.Builder with respect to '.' and '..' path segments (external dependency source not read).
RequestFactory.java path-template parsing and any validation/encoding applied to the relative URL at build time (file present in the repo listing but not read).
A concrete Retrofit service declaration plus an end-to-end request test demonstrating that a substituted ".." or "../" value results in a request to an unintended path.
Whether upstream 2.5.0 introduced an explicit traversal guard in this same method (only the version under review was read).
preconditions: Application-defined Retrofit service method uses an @Path parameter whose value is influenced by untrusted input.
The URL template places the @Path placeholder inside a path (typical usage).
For raw separators in the value, the @Path annotation is declared with encoded = true; a value containing only dots (e.g. "..") needs no encoded flag because '.' is never percent-encoded.
Downstream URL handling (OkHttp HttpUrl.resolve / newBuilder, and/or server-side normalization) does not neutralize the injected dot-segments in a way that keeps the request on the intended path.
candidates.title: Potential path traversal via @Path parameter substitution in RequestBuilder.addPathParam (no dot-segment canonicalization)
